title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.51): S is a scheme with all residue characteristics different from 2. X/S is a P^1-bundle, i.e. a Brauer–Severi conic, equivalently a form of PGL(2)_S. G = Aut_S(X). Three sets are compared:
(a) subgroup schemes V of G locally isomorphic to the Klein four-group (Z/2)^2_S;
(b) subgroup schemes Γ of G locally isomorphic to (S_4)_S;
(c) 'octahedral configurations': étale relative divisors Δ ⊂ X of degree 6 with a fixed-point-free involution σ (the 'antipodism') such that the rotation group acts compatibly on X.
The word 'icosaédrales' on p.51 is a slip, corrected there to 'octaédrales'.

This page gives the mutually inverse constructions.
- a→b: Γ = Norm_G(V). In PGL_2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠ 2, the normaliser of a Klein four-group is the octahedral group S_4.
- b→a: V is the unique normal finite étale subgroup of degree 4 of Γ. The NB notes Γ/V ≅ Aut_gr(V) ≅ Aut_S(V*) ≅ S_3, where V* = V minus the unit section is a degree-3 étale cover (the cubic resolvent).
- c→b: Γ = Aut_S(X,Δ), identified with Aut^+_{oct}(Δ), the rotation group of the combinatorial octahedron.
- a→c: each nonunit section of V gives a faithful Z/2-action on X, i.e. an involution of the conic. Its fixed locus is an étale degree-2 'axis' Δ_0. Δ is the union of the three axes (6 points), and σ swaps the two endpoints of each axis.

Corollary 1: a degree-6 étale divisor carries at most one octahedral structure, with automorphism group Aut_S(X,Δ).

Corollary 2: the category (groupoid) of oriented octahedral pairs (X,Δ), equivalently (X,V) or (X,Γ), is equivalent to that of combinatorial octahedra over S, hence to that of finite étale degree-4 covers F̃ of S. The functor sends (X,Δ) to the cover of pairs of antipodal faces. Equivalently, and characteristic-free, it uses the 3-Sylow subgroups of the automorphism group: in characteristic 3 the order-3 elements are unipotent and 'face centres' degenerate, which is presumably why Sylow subgroups are used. So the stack of octahedral conics is B S_4 = H^1(S,S_4).

Model: X = V(x^2+y^2+z^2) ⊂ P^2 over Z[1/2]. V = {±1}^3/diag ≅ (Z/2)^2 acts by sign changes, and S_4 acts by signed permutations modulo ±1. Δ is the intersection with the coordinate lines, (0,1,±i), (±i,0,1), (1,±i,0), as in the margin.

Purpose: this is the low-level input for the study of curves of type (0,4) on the next page. There, 4 points in a conic, the Klein group V_I acting with I as a torsor, and the link with 2-torsion of elliptic curves, feed the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. It is part of the 'regular polyhedra over arbitrary bases' theme announced in the Esquisse.
errors: Corollary 1, and the identification Γ = Aut_S(X,Δ) in c→b, fail on fibres of characteristic 5. There i = 2, so the octahedron {0,∞,±1,±i} is exactly P^1(F_5). Its stabiliser is PGL_2(F_5) ≅ S_5 (order 120), acting on the 6 points through the exotic embedding S_5 ⊂ S_6. Under the outer automorphism of S_6 this S_5 acts on the 15 perfect matchings with orbits of sizes 5 and 10, so the antipodal matching lies in an orbit of 5. Hence Δ = P^1(F_5) carries 5 distinct octahedral structures, and Aut(X,Δ) ≅ S_5 ≠ S_4. The correct statements need σ as part of the data, Γ = Aut_S(X,Δ,σ), or they require 5 to be invertible for the uniqueness claim. Corollary 2, phrased with σ or orientation included, survives. In characteristic 3 the stabiliser is still S_4, since it embeds in PGL_2(F_9) and must stabilise the complementary 4-set, so there is no problem there.
The orientation notation 'Δ/S ≃ H*_4S' in Corollary 2 is obscure and not explained on the page.
The page has minor slips: it calls the Klein group 'D_4', and the previous page says 'icosaédrales' for 'octaédrales'.

ideas.what: Bijection between Klein-four subgroup schemes, S_4 subgroup schemes of a form of PGL_2, and octahedral configurations (6 points with antipodism) in a conic, over any base with 2 invertible
ideas.modern_name: Classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2 / octahedral forms; stack of octahedral conics ≅ B S_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein (classical, over C); Serre and others for Galois-cohomological versions (S_4 ⊂ PGL_2, octahedral extensions)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to a theory of regular polyhedra over arbitrary rings, without details

ideas.what: Equivalence of oriented octahedral pairs (X,Δ) with degree-4 finite étale covers via antipodal face pairs, or 3-Sylow subgroups (characteristic-free)
ideas.modern_name: H^1(S,S_4) ↔ quartic étale algebras; conic attached to an S_4-torsor via S_4 → PGL_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / Galois theory of quartics (Serre, Topics in Galois Theory, for the S_4 → PGL_2 lifting context)

ideas.what: Model octahedral conic x^2+y^2+z^2=0 over Z[1/2] with sign-change Klein group and the 6 coordinate points
ideas.modern_name: standard model of octahedral symmetry on a conic

missed.claim: The page's uniqueness statement for octahedral structures implicitly assumes residue characteristic ≠ 5. In characteristic 5 the octahedron degenerates to P^1(F_5) with symmetry group S_5 and 5 octahedral structures. This is an exceptional-characteristic phenomenon in the 'regular polyhedra over Z' programme that the page does not notice.
missed.quote: Pour un diviseur étale de degré 6 Δ dans X il existe au plus une structure octaédrale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only a correction. Anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's polyhedra-over-Z theory, or arithmetic dessins in Esquisse, must add σ to the data or invert 5. The phenomenon itself (PGL_2(F_5) ≅ S_5 and the exotic S_5 ⊂ S_6) is well known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean scheme-theoretic version of classical facts (Klein group, octahedral group, union of axes) together with the standard equivalence with B S_4. It is a documented instance of the 'regular polyhedra over arbitrary bases' theme from Esquisse, and the characteristic-free use of 3-Sylows is a nice touch. However, nothing here is genuinely new to specialists, and Corollary 1 even has a gap in characteristic 5.
transcription_corrections: '(D_4)_S' in a) on the previous page denotes the Klein four-group (Z/2)^2, written elsewhere as E_{2^2}.
'V* = V_1 (sections unités)' should read roughly 'V* = V \ 1 (sections non unités)', i.e. the nontrivial sections.
'Aut^*_S(X,Δ)' in Corollary 1 is most likely Aut^+_S(X,Δ) or simply Aut_S(X,Δ).
'Δ dans X_2' should read 'Δ dans X/S'.
The model's group: '{±1}^3/diag ≃ V_{(0,1,0)}(F_2)' is probably intended as the Klein group, i.e. {±1}^3 modulo the diagonal.
'Aut^+_{loc}' near the bottom should be 'Aut^+_{fact}' or 'Aut^+_{S-oct}'.
The margin lists the six distinguished points: (0,1,±i), (±i,0,1), (1,±i,0).
